lines.en: In Italy, it’s called il gioco del cucù.
lines.zh: 在意大利，这个游戏叫 il gioco del cucù。

lines.en: Palestinians say ba’ ’éno.
lines.zh: 巴勒斯坦人说 ba’ ’éno。

lines.en: And in Japan it’s inai-inai...
lines.zh: 在日本则是 inai-inai……

lines.en: ba!
lines.zh: ba！

lines.en: But in every language, the response is usually the same.
lines.zh: 但在每一种语言里，孩子们的反应通常都一样。

lines.en: Peek-a-boo is a near-universal source of laughter and connection for infants and adults— it’s the first game that almost everyone plays.
lines.zh: 对婴儿和大人来说，躲猫猫几乎是全世界共通的笑声与亲密来源——它是几乎每个人都玩过的第一个游戏。

lines.en: So what is it about this goofy game that babies love so much?
lines.zh: 那么这个傻乎乎的游戏，到底有什么让宝宝这么着迷？

lines.en: While infants develop at different rates, many cognitive and motor abilities emerge in a certain order.
lines.zh: 虽然每个婴儿的发育速度不同，但许多认知和运动能力的出现是有先后顺序的。

lines.en: For example, while 6-month-olds can typically grab things— and then promptly drop them— walking and talking generally begin around 12 months.
lines.zh: 比方说，六个月大的宝宝通常能抓住东西——然后马上就扔掉——而走路和说话一般要到十二个月左右才开始。

lines.en: This timeline was first formally charted in 1936 by Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget.
lines.zh: 这条发展时间表，最早由瑞士心理学家让·皮亚杰在一九三六年正式整理出来。

lines.en: And while most modern researchers agree this process is more fluid than Piaget believed, the early developments he identified are key for understanding peek-a-boo.
lines.zh: 虽然今天多数研究者认为这个过程比皮亚杰以为的更灵活，但他指出的那些早期发育节点，正是理解躲猫猫的关键。

lines.en: First is face processing.
lines.zh: 首先是面孔识别。

lines.en: This happens almost immediately— newborns as young as two days old can recognize their caregivers’ faces.
lines.zh: 这几乎是立刻就有的能力——出生才两天的婴儿，就能认出照顾者的脸。

lines.en: Then, around 6 to 10 weeks, babies will begin social smiling— this is when they notice nearby laughing or smiling faces and start to mimic them.
lines.zh: 接着，大约在六到十周，宝宝开始出现「社会性微笑」——他们会注意到旁边有人笑，然后跟着模仿。

lines.en: At 2 to 4 months, they may begin to understand cause and effect.
lines.zh: 两到四个月时，他们可能开始理解因果关系。

lines.en: And finally, between 4 and 7 months they learn object permanence.
lines.zh: 最后，在四到七个月之间，他们学会了「客体永久性」。

lines.en: Piaget described this as the understanding that people and objects continue to exist even when you can’t see them.
lines.zh: 皮亚杰对它的描述是：明白人和东西即使看不见了，也依然继续存在。

lines.en: So before this period, “out of sight” can literally mean “out of mind”— making hiding your face akin to a magic trick.
lines.zh: 所以在这个阶段之前，「看不见」字面上就等于「想不到」——把脸藏起来，就跟变魔术一样神奇。

lines.en: Before object permanence, this disappearing act can range from confusing to pleasantly surprising.
lines.zh: 在有了客体永久性之前，这种消失有时让人困惑，有时又是个惊喜。

lines.en: But by 9 months, these developments are working together for peak peek-a-boo performance.
lines.zh: 但到九个月大时，这些能力凑到一起，迎来了躲猫猫的最佳状态。

lines.en: At this age, infants can focus on the game longer, predict the timing of the reveal, and even look for the hidden object or person.
lines.zh: 这个年纪的婴儿能更久地专注在游戏上，预测「哇」一声出现的时机，甚至会主动去找藏起来的东西或人。

lines.en: And since infants learn about the world through play, peek-a-boo is one of their first teachers.
lines.zh: 既然婴儿是通过玩耍来认识世界的，躲猫猫就成了他们最早的老师之一。

lines.en: In one study, 11-month-olds were shown a barrier, the bottom of which was hidden behind a screen.
lines.zh: 在一项研究中，研究者让十一个月大的婴儿看一道障碍物，障碍物的下半部分被一块挡板遮住了。

lines.en: Then researchers rolled balls and toy cars behind the screen, removing it afterwards to show that the toys had either stopped at the barrier as expected, or, somehow, gone through it.
lines.zh: 然后研究者在挡板后面滚过小球和玩具车，之后撤掉挡板，让婴儿看到玩具要么像预想的那样停在障碍物前，要么——不知怎么回事——直接穿了过去。

lines.en: Infants shown these seemingly magical toys showed more interest in them afterwards— even ignoring new objects in favor of toys that challenged their expectations.
lines.zh: 看过这些「像是会魔法」的玩具之后，婴儿对它们的兴趣明显更大——他们甚至会丢开新玩具，转而去盯着那些打破了自己预期的玩具。

lines.en: The social expectations peek-a-boo develops may be even more important.
lines.zh: 躲猫猫培养出来的社交预期，可能还要更重要。

lines.en: The game features several hallmarks of what researchers call social play: eye contact, turn-taking, and joint attention.
lines.zh: 这个游戏具备研究者所说的「社会性游戏」的几个标志：眼神接触、轮流互动、共同注意。

lines.en: These skills are the foundation of human conversation, and since it's a conversation, what the adult does matters.
lines.zh: 这些能力是人类对话的基础，而既然它是一场对话，大人怎么做就很关键。

lines.en: Just as caregivers learn to read their infant’s cries and verbal cues, babies learn how adults respond to their behavior.
lines.zh: 正如照顾者学着读懂婴儿的哭声和发出的信号，婴儿也在学着理解大人会怎样回应自己的行为。

lines.en: Some play researchers call this back and forth “serve and return” interaction, and peek-a-boo is a prime example.
lines.zh: 一些游戏研究者把这种一来一回称作「发球与回球」式互动，躲猫猫就是最典型的例子。

lines.en: This call and response structure is also why some psychologists describe peek-a-boo as a baby’s first joke.
lines.zh: 这种一呼一应的结构，也正是有些心理学家把躲猫猫称为「婴儿的第一个笑话」的原因。

lines.en: It’s an interaction where the format is reliable, but the content is surprising.
lines.zh: 在这种互动里，套路是可靠的，内容却是出乎意外的。

lines.en: As other motor and cognitive abilities develop, this foundation of social skills and object permanence informs various kinds of play.
lines.zh: 随着其他运动和认知能力继续发展，这份社交能力与客体永久性的基础，会影响各种各样的游戏。

lines.en: Once kids begin walking and talking, peek-a-boo usually evolves into hide-and-seek— though their hiding isn’t usually very good at this age due to poor impulse control and a lack of theory of mind.
lines.zh: 孩子一旦学会走路和说话，躲猫猫通常会演变成捉迷藏——不过这个年纪他们藏得并不好，因为自控力还不行，也缺少「心理理论」。

lines.en: This is the ability to understand, imagine, and predict other people’s mental states.
lines.zh: 心理理论指的是理解、想象并预测他人心理状态的能力。

lines.en: Without it, a child might think they’re hidden simply by covering their own eyes— after all, if they can’t see you, surely you can’t see them.
lines.zh: 没有它，孩子可能以为只要捂住自己的眼睛就算藏好了——毕竟，他看不见你，那你也肯定看不见他。

lines.en: Once theory of mind develops around age 3 or 4, kids can begin playing pretend together, all occupying a shared imaginary world.
lines.zh: 心理理论大约在三到四岁发展出来，之后孩子们就能一起玩假装游戏，共同置身于一个想象出来的世界里。

lines.en: Though even the most cooperative pretend play is often sprinkled with peek-a-boo style surprises.
lines.zh: 不过即便是最配合的假装游戏，也常常点缀着躲猫猫式的意外惊喜。

lines.en: By ages 5 and 6, language expands to inform more playful negotiation, leading to games with more complicated rules.
lines.zh: 到五六岁时，语言能力扩展开来，让他们能用更有趣的方式互相商量，于是出现了规则更复杂的游戏。

lines.en: After this point, most kids’ favorite types of play are more determined by their personalities and interests than their cognitive development.
lines.zh: 这之后，多数孩子喜欢玩什么，更多取决于性格和兴趣，而不是认知发育水平。

lines.en: But no matter what play they pursue, as adults they’ll likely wind up playing peek-a-boo again— this time from an all-new perspective.
lines.zh: 但不管他们后来玩什么，长大以后多半还是会重新开始玩躲猫猫——这一次，是从一个全新的视角。
